rules.title: How scoring works
rules.roiFormula: ROI = realized net PnL ÷ total margin committed
rules.roiDef: Realized net PnL = every realized PnL booked on closing − all open and close fees − net funding fees; total margin committed = everything put in on opens and adds (not what is left after a partial close). Same definition as the ROI on the Position history page.
rules.roiClosed: A position only counts once it is <0>fully closed</0> (liquidation included); unrealized profit does not count. Every partial close is booked against the position as a whole and tallied when the last slice closes. The day it counts on is the moment it is fully closed — a position opened before the campaign still counts if it is closed during it.
rules.roiLadder: <0>Slot-based: each position counts toward exactly one tier.</0> In close order it lands in the highest tier that still has room: once the 100% tier (1 slot) is full it drops to the 60% tier (3 slots), then the 40% tier (5 slots); with all three full, every position at ≥ 40% adds +1 with no limit. Positions in the 20%~40% band only ever enter their own tier (20 slots), taking no higher slot and joining no unlimited +1. Legendary trade (≥ 300%, +25) and Sweep all three markets (≥ 50% lights a market) are judged separately, so one position can count for both.
rules.roiExample: Example: 600 margin long on BTC, close half for +200, close the rest for +150, 20 in open and close fees, 10 paid in funding → net PnL = 200 + 150 − 20 − 10 = 320, ROI = 320 ÷ 600 ≈ 53.3% → lands in the "ROI ≥ 40%" tier for +3 (the 60% tier is out of reach) and lights the crypto futures bucket of Sweep all three markets (≥ 50%).
rules.spotFormula: Realized return = (total net sale proceeds − total buy cost) ÷ total buy cost
rules.spotDef: Spot has no notion of a position, so it is counted <0>per symbol</0>: "≥ 1000 bought during the campaign" is the sum of every buy order on that symbol during the campaign, <1>no single order has to reach 1000</1>. The return counts <2>only what you have actually sold</2>: total buy cost = the cash you really paid (value + fee), net sale proceeds = the cash you really received (after fees), spot fees are 0.1% on each side, and holdings you still carry are not marked to market — the denominator is every buy ever made on that symbol, so scoring basically means selling the symbol out (net proceeds above total cost).
rules.spotStep: <0>Step-based, never taken back:</0> every multiple of 10% the realized return touches (10%, 20%, 30%…) records one qualifying unit; a unit already earned survives a later drop, and the next one takes the next step (touch 10%, fall back to 5%, return to 15% — nothing; only 20% gives you the second). Units from every symbol feed one ladder: the first 3 are +5 each, the rest +1 each (up to 20, so nothing from the 24th unit on).
rules.spotCoupon: A buy order using a discount coupon is booked at <0>what you actually paid</0>, consistently on both sides: the money saved lowers the cost and lifts the return, but threshold progress also counts what you actually paid — 800 bought at 5% off counts as 760 toward "≥ 1000", so 240 more still has to be bought.
rules.spotSymbols: Eligible symbols = all spot markets: crypto spot<0> BTC / ETH / DOGE / SOL / XRP / BNB</0>, plus every tokenized US stock on bStock<1> SNDKB SanDisk / MUB Micron / NVDAB NVIDIA / AMDB / TSLAB Tesla / MSTRB MicroStrategy / CRCLB Circle / QQQB Nasdaq / SOXLB semiconductors / SPCXB SpaceX</1>.
rules.spotExample: Example: 2002 paid for BTC spot (2000 of coin + 2 in 0.1% fees), sold out for 2402.40 net (2404.80 gross − 2.40 in 0.1% fees) → (2402.40 − 2002) ÷ 2002 = 20% = 2 units, +5 each for +10. Another 1001 paid for SNDKB SanDisk bStock (1000 of stock + 1 in fees), sold out for 2002 net (2004 gross − 2 in fees) → 100% = 10 units; the first takes the last +5 slot and the other 9 are +1 each → +24 across the two symbols.
rules.fillTime: Trade time always counts from the <0>actual fill</0> (a limit order can rest for a while — the moment it fills is what counts).
